concepts.definition: A computing paradigm that augments the real physical world by coupling digital information to everyday physical objects and environments, making information perceptually and computationally coupled to physical representations.
concepts.implication: Provides foundational paradigm for giving 'substance' and materiality to database nodes; makes abstract graph structure perceptually coupled to physical topology.

concepts.definition: Interaction grounded in phenomenological understanding where meaning arises through pre-reflective bodily engagement with the world; perception and action are inseparable, and understanding emerges from physical doing rather than abstract representation alone.
concepts.implication: Explains why spatial graph metaphors feel intuitive and learnable without explicit instruction; the body 'already knows' how to navigate through embodied spatial structures.

concepts.definition: The engagement of the user's body and the physical material world as central design dimensions; includes material properties, spatial constraints, bodily affordances, and sensorimotor feedback as features that scaffold interaction.
concepts.implication: Physical weight, texture, and constraints of nodes become design features that guide exploration without explicit instructions; material properties communicate interaction affordances.

concepts.definition: The use of spatial properties, layout, and arrangement of physical objects as primary interaction mechanisms; physical space becomes semantically meaningful and directly navigable.
concepts.implication: Metro-map spatial layout becomes directly explorable through physical manipulation; traversing physical space mirrors query traversal through database topology.

concepts.definition: Cognitive processes are fundamentally grounded in bodily interaction with the environment; abstract thought is scaffolded by sensorimotor experience, and physical action/perception precedes and enables higher-order reasoning.
concepts.implication: Physical manipulation of graph elements reduces cognitive load through embodied understanding; spatial reasoning is enhanced by kinesthetic feedback.

concepts.definition: Learning through hands-on physical manipulation of tangible objects where the body and its movements are active agents in knowledge construction; haptic interaction and kinesthetic feedback enhance knowledge transfer.
key_refs: Li et al 2022 Meta-Analysis of TEI Learning
concepts.implication: Exploring database graph through physical tangibles enables deeper learning of data relationships; users retain query patterns and structural understanding better through embodied manipulation.

concepts.definition: Interaction paradigm characterized by continuous visual/physical representation of objects, physical actions directly on those objects, rapid reversible feedback, and immediate visibility of results.
concepts.implication: Direct physical manipulation of graph nodes provides immediate feedback on query results; users see consequences of structural changes instantly.

concepts.definition: Physical and perceptual properties of objects that communicate possible actions; how material design and form 'speak' about interaction possibilities without requiring explicit instructions or labels.
concepts.implication: Node shape, texture, and weight signal their role in graph structure; edge thickness communicates relationship strength through haptic and visual affordances.

concepts.definition: Model of information-seeking behavior applying optimal foraging theory to user navigation; users follow 'information scent'—cues signaling likelihood of finding relevant information—to guide exploration decisions.
concepts.implication: Physical spatial layout provides natural information scent for graph exploration; proximity and clustering guide users toward relevant subgraphs without explicit search.

concepts.definition: Philosophical foundation asserting that perception is embodied and pre-reflective; the body engages with the world prior to conscious thought, grounding all knowledge in sensorimotor experience.
concepts.implication: Physical interaction with graph feels intuitive because it leverages pre-reflective bodily knowledge; no learning curve for basic spatial navigation.

concepts.definition: Interaction modality using physical gestures and body movements as primary input; leverages complementary processing of spatial/kinesthetic and verbal information, with gestures conveying spatial relations naturally.
concepts.implication: Gesture vocabulary for graph manipulation (rotate structures, zoom into regions, drag connections) leverages natural spatial understanding.

concepts.definition: Interaction technique enabling simultaneous multi-point contact on touch-sensitive surfaces; two-handed and multi-user manipulation enables complex spatial transformations through coordinated physical actions.
concepts.implication: Multiple database analysts can simultaneously manipulate different graph regions; natural bimanual rotation/scaling/translation of subgraphs.

concepts.definition: Computer-supported physical representations of data using tangible materials and objects; analogous to data visualization but leveraging material, spatial, and embodied properties for exploration and understanding.
concepts.implication: Database graph becomes physical network structure; nodes/edges materially represent database topology, enabling tactile exploration.

concepts.definition: Physical interfaces that dynamically alter their shape, texture, or form to represent digital state or enable different affordances; morphing materials and actuated structures create responsive physical feedback.
concepts.implication: Graph nodes can dynamically reshape to show importance, state changes, or query results; height variation shows metric prominence.

concepts.definition: Theoretical framework positing that meaning emerges in human-material interaction; physical objects are active agents shaping cognition and culture rather than passive vessels of information.
concepts.implication: Choice of physical material for nodes/edges becomes cognitive and semiotic choice; material properties influence how users perceive and reason about data.

concepts.definition: Tactile and kinesthetic feedback through electrical stimulation, vibration, mechanical resistance, or temperature; engages the sense of touch as active channel in interaction, complementing vision.
concepts.implication: Tactile feedback when manipulating nodes/edges (resistance, vibration at connection points) enriches interaction and provides confirmation of actions.

concepts.definition: Tangible interfaces designed for co-located multi-user interaction where embodied constraints and spatial layout enable collaborative problem-solving, peer learning, and negotiation without explicit communication protocols.
concepts.implication: Multiple database analysts explore graph together; shared physical interface enables peer discussion and collaborative query formulation.

concepts.definition: Design theme for tangible systems where physical embodiment and spatial constraints scaffold collaborative interaction; multiple access points and tailored representations enable natural coordination and learning.
concepts.implication: Physical graph topology naturally facilitates coordination between analysts; no need for explicit protocols—spatial arrangement guides collaborative reasoning.

concepts.definition: Paradigm shift from screen-centric computing to environment-embedded interaction; computing fades into background, enabling seamless human-world interaction without explicit focus on technology.
concepts.implication: Physical graph becomes integrated part of analyst workspace rather than isolated application; technology disappears into data exploration task.

concepts.definition: Tangible objects designed to be grasped and physically manipulated; physical interaction with handles/graspable surfaces directly controls digital state through intuitive embodied metaphor.
key_refs: Ishii & Ullmer Tangible Bits graspable category
concepts.implication: Database nodes designed as graspable objects with clear grasp points; physical position and rotation directly map to query position/properties.

concepts.definition: Digital information presented in physical form at periphery of attention; leverages embodied perception and ambient awareness to convey information without requiring conscious focus or explicit interaction.
key_refs: Ishii & Ullmer Tangible Bits ambient media
concepts.implication: Physical graph can present aggregate data properties (connectivity, density, change magnitude) as ambient properties (height variation, color gradients) perceived without active attention.

concepts.definition: Physical surfaces augmented with digital tracking, projection, and computation; real-world objects and tokens tagged with digital information create seamless hybrid interaction spaces.
concepts.implication: Physical tokens on augmented surface represent graph nodes; projected connections show relationships; manipulation updates digital query state.

concepts.definition: Design of embodied interfaces that actively engage spatial reasoning abilities (mental rotation, perspective-taking, wayfinding, spatial memory); physical interaction enhances development of spatial skills.
key_refs: Antle & Wise Embodied Interaction Spatial Skills
concepts.implication: Exploring physical graph strengthens analyst's spatial understanding of database structure; 3D spatial reasoning becomes skill developed through interaction.

concepts.definition: Embodied physical interaction reduces mental/cognitive burden by offloading abstract processing to sensorimotor and kinesthetic systems; working memory load decreases through distributed cognition across body and environment.
concepts.implication: Physical graph exploration reduces working memory load compared to screen-only analysis; analysts can focus on high-level patterns rather than low-level navigation.

concepts.definition: Meaningful correspondence between physical properties/structure and digital meaning; physical affordances and layout communicate conceptual structure and enable intuitive understanding.
concepts.implication: Physical arrangement of nodes mirrors database topology; edge connections physically represent data relationships; traversal metaphor matches query/exploration patterns.

concepts.definition: Tangible/physical interaction enabling remote users to have embodied presence in shared physical space; combines telepresence with tangible manipulation for distributed collaborative embodied interaction.
concepts.implication: Remote data analysts can collaborate on physical graph with embodied presence; distributed teams experience shared spatial reasoning through remotely-controlled tangible proxies.

concepts.definition: Systematic nested validation model for visualization design: domain problem abstraction, data/task abstraction, visual encoding idiom, and algorithm; emphasizes rigorous task analysis and interaction technique design.
concepts.implication: Physical graph design follows systematic task abstraction; interaction techniques chosen based on analytical tasks rather than ad-hoc aesthetic decisions.

concepts.definition: Systems that sense and adapt to environmental/user/location context; interaction behavior and information presentation adjust based on contextual signals enabling location-aware and situation-appropriate responses.
concepts.implication: Physical graph display adapts to analyst location, role, task context; different analysts see different representations based on their contextual needs.

concepts.definition: Affordances that change over time or in response to interaction; physical objects morph to present different interaction possibilities as state changes, enabling responsive and contextual guidance.
concepts.implication: Nodes actuate to signal importance or state; edges raise to highlight connection paths; physical affordances invite interaction with high-priority data.

concepts.definition: Paradigm where physical tangible objects serve as proxies for data elements; user manipulations of tangibles directly drive analytical queries, filtering, and transformations on underlying datasets.
concepts.implication: Users grasp and manipulate physical nodes to issue queries; moving node position filters; rotating node orientation changes analysis perspective; manipulation becomes query language.

concepts.definition: Interaction combining physical tangible objects with digital augmentation in mixed/augmented reality environments; tangible objects mediate digital interaction in hybrid physical-digital space.
concepts.implication: Physical tokens tracked in AR space; digital information layer shows connectivity/properties on physical topology; real and virtual seamlessly integrated.

concepts.definition: Empirical characterization of gesture performance on touch-enabled displays; systematic design and evaluation of gesture vocabulary for accuracy, speed, and learnability.
concepts.implication: Gesture vocabulary for graph navigation on touch-augmented tangible surfaces designed based on empirical performance data.

concepts.definition: Psychological and emotional attachment to physical artifacts; perception of fragility, safety, ownership, and aesthetic appeal influences interaction patterns and user commitment.
concepts.implication: Material choice and affordance design evoke emotional investment in graph analysis; users care more about careful manipulation when objects feel valuable.

concepts.definition: Using digital fabrication technologies (3D printing, laser cutting, CNC) to rapidly prototype and customize tangible interfaces; enables domain-specific physical designs tailored to application needs.
concepts.implication: Custom tangible graph nodes fabricated for specific database domains; node shape encodes schema type; edge form encodes relationship semantics.

concepts.definition: Co-design methodology involving end-users as active partners in tangible interface creation; stakeholders and domain experts shape physical interaction possibilities and representations.
concepts.implication: Database engineers and analysts co-design physical graph representation; end-user expertise shapes node affordances and connection representations.

concepts.definition: Premier international peer-reviewed venue for tangible/embedded/embodied interaction research (since 2007); establishes empirical evidence base and community standards for tangible and embodied design.
key_refs: Li et al Meta-Analysis of TEI
concepts.implication: MetroGraph design grounded in 15+ years of peer-reviewed TEI research community standards and empirical findings; evidence base for embodied interaction efficacy.

concepts.definition: Use of spatial position, proximity, and arrangement as primary encoding mechanism for data semantics; spatial relationships become semantically meaningful rather than arbitrary, enabling direct spatial reasoning about data.
concepts.implication: Database topology directly encoded in physical layout; node proximity mirrors edge connectivity; traversal path encodes query logic.

concepts.definition: Design strategy leveraging fundamental embodied understanding (spatial, kinesthetic, sensorimotor) to create intuitive mappings between physical actions and digital operations.
concepts.implication: Graph rotation in hand parallels mental rotation of structure; path tracing matches query traversal; connection pulling mirrors relationship formation.
